question:
Given is a circle with centre at C. A, B and D are the points on the circumference. Find ∠ABC.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/799a556b718f11bcde00fff5ad2e5a3c1cf8982ad5f2148fcfa7ba14b1e6cfae.png]
solution:
**Given:**

A circle with center at C. A, B, and D are points on the circumference.

∠BCD = 126°

∠ADC = 33°

**Formula used:**

The angle subtended by an arc at the center is twice the angle subtended at any point on the remaining part of the circumference.

**Calculation:**

∠BAC is subtended by the arc BD at the center.

∠BCD is subtended by the same arc BD on the circumference.

⇒ ∠BAD = (1/2) × ∠BCD

⇒ ∠BAD = (1/2) × 126° = 63°

Draw a line AC then,

BC = CD = AC = radius of circle.

In ΔACD, AC = CD

So, it is an isosceles triangle,

∠CAD = ∠ADC = 33∘ 

∠BAC = ∠BAD - ∠CAD

∠BAC = 63∘ - 33∘ = 30∘ 

In ΔBAC, BC = CA

So, it is an isosceles triangle.

∠ABC = ∠BAC = 30∘ 

**∴ The correct answer is 30∘ **
